title: GMN orbits 2019-2026 confirm Taurid resonant swarm returns in 2022 and 2025; the 2025 fireball-class rate was 0.88 times the 2022 rate, against a prediction that 2022 was the last strong return
abstract: We tested published predictions for the Taurid resonant swarm (Taurid meteoroids in the 7:2 resonance with Jupiter) with Global Meteor Network (GMN) orbits from 2019 to 2026. We used solar longitude 213-234 degrees and normalised with sporadic meteors. The Asher and Clube (1993) model lists 2022 (offset +17 degrees in mean anomaly) and 2025 (-25 degrees) as swarm years. These two years had the two highest of eight resonant-branch rates (chance 1/28). The GMN s-Taurid rate was 92.5 and 50.9 per 100 sporadic meteors, against 4.5 to 5.6 in 2020-2024 and 2026. Precise Southern Taurid orbits had a narrow peak at a = 2.21 au in both years. This is 0.05 au below the nominal 2.256 au, probably because of a GMN speed bias. The fraction of these orbits in the band 2.15-2.30 au was 0.61-0.63, against 0.10-0.15 in other years. The regular Southern Taurid rate did not change. The excess increased by a factor of 1.4-1.6 for each magnitude brighter. For fireball-class meteors (magnitude -2 or brighter), the excess was 30 times (2022) and 26 times (2025) the background. The 2025/2022 ratio was 0.88 (95% CI 0.56-1.36). Thus the data do not support the Egal et al. (2022) statement that 2022 was the last strong return until the mid-late 2030s. Faint meteors had a 2025 rate of approximately one half of the 2022 rate. A Gaussian fit in mean-anomaly offset gives a centre of +5 degrees and a sigma of 24 degrees. It also fits a weak 2019 excess (+58 degrees, 8 percent of 2022). From this fit we predict 0.36 times the 2022 level for November 2029 and 1.1 times for 2032. Limitations: only two swarm years; the GMN network grew by a factor of 10; GMN shower labels and the orbit band are not fully independent; the profile fit is exploratory; and the forecast intervals include only the sampling error.

display.caption: Resonant Taurid rates per 100 sporadic meteors (20-35 km/s) at solar longitude 213-234 degrees for each year 2019-2026. Left: GMN s-Taurid (STS) label. Right: precise Southern Taurid orbits with semi-major axis 2.15-2.30 au. Orange: swarm years listed by Asher and Clube (1993). Numbers: offset of the swarm centre in mean anomaly. Bars: 95% night-block bootstrap intervals. 2026 has data only to 225.3 degrees.

Left: semi-major axis of precise Southern Taurid complex orbits (sigma(a) < 0.02 au). The swarm years 2022 and 2025 have a narrow peak near 2.21 au. The dotted line is the nominal 7:2 resonance. Right: geocentric speed against solar longitude. The swarm-year meteors make the resonant s-Taurid track.

Excess s-Taurid rate against the predicted offset of the swarm centre (Delta M) for 2019-2026, with a Gaussian fit (centre +5 degrees, sigma 24 degrees; grey: bootstrap 95% band). Violet triangles: forecasts for November 2029, 2032, 2035 and 2039 from the same model.
